entries.what_happened: The manuscript 'Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes' claims a ZFC proof of its Theorem 'Uniform eventual categoricity'. For every infinite cardinal λ there is a cardinal μ(λ) ≥ λ such that, for every AEC K with LS(K) ≤ λ, if K is categorical in some κ ≥ μ(λ) then K is categorical in every κ' ≥ μ(λ). The threshold depends only on λ, not on K. Categoricity includes the existence of a model. The manuscript first proves a qualitative version (an AEC categorical in unboundedly many cardinals is categorical on a tail) and says the uniform version follows from it by a set-coding reduction over the set of codes of AECs with LS number at most λ. The companion manuscript 'A CH obstruction to a prescribed categoricity threshold' is cited in the introduction only as context. It bears on this problem only indirectly. Under CH it builds an AEC with LS ℵ₀ that is categorical in every μ ≥ Λ but has two nonisomorphic models at h(ℵ₀) = ℶ_{ω₂}, so the explicit threshold h(LS(K)) fails for that class. It does not contradict an existential threshold.
entries.delivers: Gives the list's statement in ZFC, with no amalgamation, joint embedding, tameness, no-maximal-models, large-cardinal or GCH-type hypothesis, and with the same threshold in premise and conclusion. Compared with the list: (a) the manuscript quantifies over infinite λ only. Its LS number is always infinite by definition (ℓ ≥ |τ|+ℵ₀ is infinite), so the finite cases of 'every cardinal λ' are vacuous under its conventions. (b) It asserts categoricity at or above μ(λ), which implies the list's version with 'above μ(λ)'. The manuscript says this resolves Shelah's conjecture positively. The threshold is existential and is not given numerically. My inference from reading both manuscripts, which neither states: under CH, μ(ℵ₀) must exceed ℶ_{ω₂}, because the CH companion's AEC with LS ℵ₀ is categorical in Λ but not at ℶ_{ω₂}. The two claims are consistent.
entries.remains: Nothing in the list's statement. The manuscript gives no explicit or numerical μ(λ). It treats the explicit-threshold question (Shelah, Conjecture N.4.3(1)(b)) as separate, and the list's statement does not ask for it.
entries.direction: proves the conjecture (existential uniform threshold, ZFC)
entries.doubts: (1) The paper has 14 sections. I read the introduction, the proof overview, the final cardinal-transfer section and the closing reduction, but not sections 02 to 13. The uniform form depends on the set-coding reduction (Proposition found:uniform-reduction) and on a forward-referenced existence of a categorical pointed level (Proposition geom:pointed-levels). I did not check either. (2) The introduction says Boney and Vasey found a gap in the unrestricted syntactic characterization in Shelah's Chapter IV, and that their valid variants need exponentiation or cofinality assumptions that do not cover all starting cardinals. The manuscript says it proves the needed reversal of strong maps directly (Theorem found:reversal). I did not verify this. (3) The introduction contrasts this result with earlier positive results (Boney 2014, Grossberg–VanDieren, Shelah–Vasey) that needed amalgamation, tameness, strongly compact cardinals or WGCH. The claim is therefore strong relative to that literature, and I did not verify its proof.

entries.what_happened: The manuscript 'Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes' says in its introduction that its uniform theorem applies to sentences of L_{ω1,ω} in countable languages. For such a sentence φ, one chooses a countable fragment containing φ and orders models by elementarity for that fragment. The text says this gives an AEC with LS number ℵ₀ (citing Boney–Vasey 2017 survey, Example 2.0.2), with the same models and isomorphisms. So one threshold μ(ℵ₀) serves all such sentences: if φ is categorical in some κ ≥ μ(ℵ₀), it is categorical in every κ' ≥ μ(ℵ₀). The same introduction says the prescribed ℶ_{ω1} threshold of the classical infinitary formulation 'remains a separate question' (Boney–Vasey 2015, Conjecture 1.1). The companion manuscript 'A CH obstruction to a prescribed categoricity threshold' concerns general AECs, not L_{ω1,ω} sentences. Its threshold is h(ℵ₀) = ℶ_{(2^ℵ₀)⁺}, which under CH is ℶ_{ω₂}, not ℶ_{ω1}. Its counterexample is not claimed to be L_{ω1,ω}-definable. It is the closer of the two to the bullet's wording, since it calls its target 'the prescribed-threshold form of Shelah's categoricity conjecture', but it does not address the bullet's threshold.
entries.delivers: An existential-threshold version for countable-vocabulary L_{ω1,ω} sentences: categoricity in some cardinal at or above μ(ℵ₀) implies categoricity in every cardinal at or above μ(ℵ₀), where μ(ℵ₀) is an unspecified cardinal. Against the bullet's parts: (1) scope is covered only for countable vocabularies, which the manuscript states explicitly; (2) the premise is read as 'categorical in some κ at or above the threshold', the usual Shelah reading, which the manuscript uses; (4) the conclusion covers all cardinals at or above the threshold. Part (3) is not covered: the threshold is not the Hanf number, and the manuscript does not say it is. The manuscript does not claim to settle the classical form.
entries.remains: The bullet's threshold, the Hanf number of L_{ω1,ω}. The manuscript supplies only the unspecified μ(ℵ₀) and names the ℶ_{ω1} version as open. Uncountable vocabularies are not covered. Read literally with the Hanf number as threshold, the bullet is left open by this family.
entries.direction: proves a special case: existential threshold (not the Hanf number) for countable-vocabulary L_{ω1,ω} sentences
entries.conditional_on: The AEC step is cited, not proved: that the fragment-ordered class is an AEC with LS number ℵ₀ (Boney–Vasey 2017 survey, Example 2.0.2). The corollary also depends on the uniform theorem of the 'Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes' manuscript.
entries.doubts: The reduction is one paragraph. The text asserts that the models and isomorphisms are unchanged and that the same μ(ℵ₀) works for all sentences. It does not check the AEC axioms (union, coherence, LS) for the fragment ordering, nor that the AEC's models are the sentence's models. I did not check the cited survey example.
